Where it began

Matthew Scott Wade arrived on Boxing Day 1987 in Hobart, into a family steeped in Australian football. His father, Scott Wade, played for Hawthorn in the VFL and later ran AFL Tasmania for many years, and the Collingwood defender Jeremy Howe is his cousin.

Young Matthew was good at both games. He was vice-captain of the Tassie Mariners football side, sharing the field with several future AFL players, and he represented Tasmania in junior cricket before playing for Australia at the 2006 Under-19 World Cup. Cricket won.

The player

With Tim Paine ahead of him behind the stumps in Tasmania, Wade moved to Victoria in 2007 and within two years was their first-choice keeper. In the 2009/10 Sheffield Shield final he walked in with Victoria at five for 60 and made 96, earning the man of the match award as they won by 457 runs.

His Test debut came in Barbados in April 2012, and his first Test century followed later on that tour in Roseau. He went on to play 36 Tests from 2012 to 2021, scoring 1,613 runs at 29.87 with four hundreds. Behind the stumps he took 63 catches and made 11 stumpings.

What made him special

Wade was a fighter. He spent three and a half years out of the Test side and came back, and in 2019 he played all five Ashes Tests in England, making 337 runs with two centuries. The best of them, 117 at The Oval, was his highest Test score. When a side was in a hole, he seemed to enjoy the climb out.

The white-ball game suited him too. He was player of the match on both his T20 and one-day international breakthroughs against India, captained Australia in T20 internationals, and was a key part of the side that won the 2021 T20 World Cup. His Test batting average sat just under thirty, but few keepers have been better company in a tight finish.

Away from the middle

He went home to Tasmania in 2017, took the gloves there again and in 2018 earned a place in the Shield's team of the year. He later led both Tasmania and the Hobart Hurricanes, and played in leagues from the Indian Premier League to The Hundred and the Pakistan Super League. He left red-ball cricket in 2024, international cricket in October that year and the Big Bash in 2026.

And finally

His maiden one-day hundred, against Pakistan at the Gabba in 2017, arrived on the very last ball of the innings. A fumble in the field on the ball before gave him two runs and kept him on strike. Some batsmen plan their centuries; Wade simply refused to run out of time.
